content_html:
Stop Your AI From Breaking Working Code

Rules and prompts that keep Claude Code, Cursor, and Codex from wrecking things that already worked. Everything here is copy-paste. Explanations kept to a minimum.

한국어 →

The first two weeks feel like magic. Then the codebase grows past what the model can hold at once, and it starts fixing A while breaking B.

That isn't a skill problem. It's a structure problem — which means prompting harder won't fix it. Constraints will.

Everything on this page is free. If you want the long version afterwards, there's a 25-page field manual — $19 · don't buy it if you already write your own hooks and subagents

The one thing to do tonight

Create CLAUDE.md in your project root and paste this. Claude Code reads it automatically at the start of every conversation.

(Cursor → .cursorrules, Codex/Copilot → AGENTS.md. Same content.)

# Project

## What this is
[one sentence]

## Current state
[what works, what doesn't yet]

## Do not touch
- [file/folder] — [why]

## Rules
- Do not modify files I did not ask you to modify
- Do not refactor working code without being asked
- If unsure, say "I don't know". Never present a guess as fact
- Never report something as done without verifying it

Why "do not" instead of "please do"

Please write clean code does nothing. There's no threshold for clean, so no behavior changes.

Prohibitions have a clear edge. They land immediately.

❌ No effect ⭕ Works
Write clean code Do not modify files I didn't ask about
Be careful Do not merge without tests
Keep it organized Do not touch legacy/

5 prompts that prevent breakage

1. Before letting it change anything

Don't write code yet. First tell me which files you'd touch
and where the risky parts are.

Starting with "fix it" means the model edits things it can't itself account for. Getting the plan first kills most collateral damage.

2. When you're scared it'll break something

Before changing this, tell me what else is affected by it.

Works better than scolding. It ends up confessing: "ah, this is coupled to the character class."

3. When you get "Done!"

Don't tell me it works. Write a test and show me it passes.

Models are bad at catching their own errors. They review with the same assumptions they built with — so a wrong assumption survives both passes. "Looks good" is an opinion. A passing test is evidence.

4. Before starting a fresh chat

Summarize: what's done / what's next / what we tried and abandoned.
Write it so a fresh session can continue from that alone.

"What we abandoned" is the important part. Without it, the new session confidently proposes the exact approach that just failed.

5. The line for your rules file

Do not modify files I did not ask you to modify.

Single highest-value line in the file.

Make the important files untouchable

CLAUDE.md is advice. Long conversation, priority drops, it edits the file anyway.

guard/ is a hook. It runs before the tool call and refuses it.

Blocked by guard.py: .env
It matches the pattern '.env' listed in .claude/protected.txt.

Two minutes to install, no dependencies, and it can't be talked out of it. List what must never be touched in .claude/protected.txt and stop worrying about it.

Context rots

Long sessions get worse, and it isn't your imagination.

As the conversation grows, abandoned directions and corrected mistakes all keep counting as current context. The signal gets buried in its own history.

Start a fresh session every 3–5 tasks. Run prompt #4 before you close.

Anger is the signal

If you're asking for the same thing a third time, stop rewording the request and change the window. That session can no longer produce the answer. Pushing harder only raises your blood pressure.

Make everything reversible

If git feels like a wall, you don't need the commands. Just say:

Before starting:   save the current state
When it breaks:    restore the state you saved

Nobody plays a game without saving. Same rule.

One rule for permissions

Can Ctrl+Z undo this?

Just let it run Always confirm first
Reading, searching, analyzing Deleting
Local edits (if you saved state) Deploying
Drafting Sending email / messages
Running tests Payments, orders

All-or-nothing is the worst setting. Gate the irreversible, free the rest.

Kill switch

Put this in your rules file:

If a file named STOP.txt exists in this folder, halt all work immediately.

One file stops everything. With it you can leave things running. Without it you can't.

Failures are training data

Every time the model gets something wrong, append that sentence to your rules file.

Rules you imagine in advance are mostly useless. Rules extracted from actual breakage are the ones that hold.

## Known traps
- Stock deduction in order_service.py sits outside the transaction. Known, leaving it
- test_payment.py hits the live API. Don't run it casually
- We tried the event-driven approach and dropped it. Do not propose it again

Do this for a week and it stops repeating itself.

Summary

  • Keep the explanation in a file (CLAUDE.md)
  • Get the plan before the code
  • Save state so you can roll back
  • Whoever built it doesn't get to grade it
  • Gate only what's irreversible
  • "Done" means evidence, not a claim

Don't try to adopt all of it. Write the CLAUDE.md tonight. That one file changes tomorrow.

If Claude Code limits are full, Codex is waiting for reset, automations are running, and the payment notification is still silent, the bottleneck may not be automation. It may be the offer.

DEV launch article: https://dev.to/taehyeon_jeon_5618e0c8332/if-your-ai-automations-are-running-but-revenue-is-still-0-diagnose-the-offer-first-5fo1

No income guarantee. No custom implementation. A self-execution kit for validating a paid AI automation offer before buying another tool.

The longer version

Everything above is free and always will be. If it was useful and you want the full treatment, there's a 25-page field manual that goes deeper:

Working With Claude Code — Field Manual · $19 · PDF

  • Approval gates, hooks, and kill switches in detail
  • Skills — turning repeated instructions into assets
  • Cost control and when not to build an autonomous loop
  • 7 copy-paste templates + a symptom → cause → fix table
  • The chapter on not fooling yourself about results

Don't buy it if you already design your own hooks, skills, and subagents. You'd learn little. The README above is the useful half for most people.

Contributing

If you have a line that actually works for you, open a PR or an issue. Real ones only — rules that survived contact with a real codebase.

Stuck right now?

  • Ask a question → https://avenna01-ceo.github.io/makhyeoss/
  • Threads (KR) → @k_aria26

Free. If I can solve it I will; if I can't I'll say so.

content_html_zh:
阻止你的人工智能破坏工作代码

规则和提示可以防止 Claude Code、Cursor 和 Codex 破坏已经起作用的东西。 这里的一切都是复制粘贴的。 解释保持在最低限度。

한국어 →

前两周感觉就像魔法一样。 然后代码库的增长超出了模型可以容纳的范围，它开始修复 A，同时破坏 B。

这不是技能问题。 这是一个结构问题——这意味着更努力的提示并不能解决问题。 约束会。

该页面上的所有内容都是免费的。 如果您之后想要长版本，有一本 25 页的现场手册 — 19 美元 · 如果您已经编写了自己的钩子和子代理，请不要购买它

今晚要做的一件事

在项目根目录中创建 CLAUDE.md 并将其粘贴。 克劳德·科德在每次对话开始时都会自动阅读它。

（光标 → .cursorrules，Codex/Copilot → AGENTS.md。 内容相同。）

# Project

## What this is
[one sentence]

## Current state
[what works, what doesn't yet]

## Do not touch
- [file/folder] — [why]

## Rules
- Do not modify files I did not ask you to modify
- Do not refactor working code without being asked
- If unsure, say "I don't know". Never present a guess as fact
- Never report something as done without verifying it

为什么“不要”而不是“请这样做”

请编写干净的代码，什么也不做。 清洁没有门槛，因此行为不会改变。

禁令有明显的优势。 他们立即着陆。

❌没有效果 ⭕ Works
编写干净的代码 不要修改我没有询问的文件
当心 未经测试请勿合并
保持井井有条 不要碰遗产/

5个防止破损的提示

1. 在让它改变任何事情之前

Don't write code yet. First tell me which files you'd touch
and where the risky parts are.

从“修复它”开始意味着模型会编辑它本身无法解释的内容。 首先制定计划可以消除大部分附带损害。

2. 当你害怕的时候它会破坏一些东西

Before changing this, tell me what else is affected by it.

比责骂更有效。 它最终承认：“啊，这与角色类别有关。”

3. 当你得到“完成！”时

Don't tell me it works. Write a test and show me it passes.

模型不善于发现自己的错误。 他们使用与建立时相同的假设进行审查——因此错误的假设在两次传递中都会存在。 “看起来不错”是一种意见。 通过测试就是证据。

4. 在开始新的聊天之前

Summarize: what's done / what's next / what we tried and abandoned.
Write it so a fresh session can continue from that alone.

“我们放弃了什么”是重要的部分。 如果没有它，新会议就会自信地提出刚刚失败的方法。

5. 规则文件的行

Do not modify files I did not ask you to modify.

文件中单个最高值行。

让重要文件不可触及

CLAUDE.md 是建议。 长时间的对话，优先级下降，它无论如何都会编辑文件。

Guard/ 是一个钩子。 它在工具调用之前运行并拒绝它。

Blocked by guard.py: .env
It matches the pattern '.env' listed in .claude/protected.txt.

两分钟即可安装，没有依赖项，并且无法谈论它。 列出 .claude/protected.txt 中绝对不能触及的内容，并停止担心它。

上下文腐烂

长时间的训练会变得更糟，这不是你的想象。

随着对话的深入，放弃的方向和纠正的错误都将继续算作当前上下文。 信号被埋藏在它自己的历史中。

每完成 3-5 个任务就开始一次新的会话。 关闭之前运行提示#4。

愤怒是信号

如果您第三次提出同样的要求，请停止改写请求并更改窗口。 该会议无法再给出答案。 用力推动只会导致血压升高。

让一切都可以逆转

如果 git 感觉像一堵墙，那么您就不需要这些命令。 就说：

Before starting:   save the current state
When it breaks:    restore the state you saved

没有人会在不保存的情况下玩游戏。 同样的规则。

权限的一条规则

Ctrl+Z 可以撤消此操作吗？
就让它运行吧 始终先确认
阅读、搜索、分析 正在删除
本地编辑（如果您保存了状态） 部署
起草 发送电子邮件/消息
运行测试 付款、订单

全有或全无是最糟糕的设置。 关闭不可逆转的大门，释放其余的。

终止开关

将其放入您的规则文件中：

If a file named STOP.txt exists in this folder, halt all work immediately.

一个文件就能阻止一切。 有了它，您就可以让一切继续运行。 没有它你就不能。

失败是训练数据

每次模型出现问题时，将该句子附加到您的规则文件中。

你预先想象的规则大多是没有用的。 从实际破坏中提取的规则才是有效的。

## Known traps
- Stock deduction in order_service.py sits outside the transaction. Known, leaving it
- test_payment.py hits the live API. Don't run it casually
- We tried the event-driven approach and dropped it. Do not propose it again

这样做一周，这种情况就不会再重演。

概括

  • 将说明保存在文件中 (CLAUDE.md)
  • 先获取计划再获取代码
  • 保存状态以便您可以回滚
  • 无论是谁建造了它都无法对其进行评分
  • 只控制不可逆转的事情
  • “完成”意味着证据，而不是主张

不要试图全部采用。 今晚写 CLAUDE.md。 该文件明天会更改。
